title: Artificial Intelligence and Intangible Cultural Heritage. Mapping terra (in)cognita
content:
On 11 September 2026, Hanna Schreiber will deliver the keynote “Artificial Intelligence and Intangible Cultural Heritage. Mapping terra (in)cognita)” at the international conference Generative Traditions: Living Heritage and Artificial Intelligence. New Horizons – Exploring Cultural Possibilities in Athens, Greece. The keynote is scheduled for 10:15–10:45.

The presentation explores the emerging relationship between artificial intelligence and intangible cultural heritage, focusing in particular on the conceptual, ethical and governance questions arising at their intersection.

The keynote presents work prepared in cooperation with our UNESCO Chair Team Members: Bartosz Pieliński and Julia Krzesicka-Haberko.

The conference is organised by the Hellenic Ministry of Culture, through the Directorate of Modern Cultural Heritage, in cooperation with UNESCO. It brings together communities, scholars, cultural professionals, research institutions and policymakers to discuss both the opportunities and the challenges presented by artificial intelligence in relation to living heritage.
